response.title: My floor-rising screen needs to sit about 10 inches higher to line up with the projector. What can I put it on besides mounting it to the wall?
response.answer:
You have several good options for raising a floor-rising projector screen by about 10 inches without mounting it to the wall.

Because floor-rising screens can be heavy and have a relatively high center of gravity when extended, I'd prioritize a long, low, sturdy platform that supports the entire screen housing.

4 options I'd consider
Shop

1. Custom wooden riser platform

Best overall

A 10-inch-high wooden platform, made from plywood and a braced frame. You can match its width to the screen housing and paint it to blend into the room.

Best for: A permanent, clean-looking setup.

Shop

2. Low-profile TV console

Look for a media cabinet approximately 10 inches tall, with a solid top that supports the entire screen housing.

Best for: A finished furniture look, with storage for AV equipment.

Shop

3. Metal equipment platform

A heavy-duty steel platform or low stage riser with a rated load capacity and a wide, stable base.

Best for: Strength, durability, and a more industrial look.

Shop

4. Solid-top low bench

A sturdy bench around 10 inches high can work, provided it has a rigid, level top and won't tip when the screen extends.

Best for: A furniture-style solution without custom construction.

What I'd recommend

I'd choose a 10-inch-high custom wooden platform, ideally with a black finish to match the screen housing. It can look like part of the home theater rather than an improvised stand.

A few important details:

Support the full length of the screen's base, not just the ends, unless the manufacturer specifies support points.

Make sure the platform is level, rigid, and cannot slide or tip.

Check whether your screen requires anti-tip restraints or anchoring, even when freestanding.

Keep the screen's rising mechanism and any bottom vents unobstructed.

Two questions that would help me recommend something you can actually buy:

How wide is your floor-rising screen housing — roughly 80, 100, or 120 inches?

Would you prefer something that looks like furniture, or a simple platform that's inexpensive and functional?

With those details, I can narrow it down to ready-made options that are close to 10 inches tall.
